contrary_evidence: The 2026 regional conflict still curtailed trade and oil exports despite Saudi logistics redundancy; the East-West route therefore reduces but does not eliminate Gulf exposure.
Female participation fell from 36.3% in 2025Q1 to 34.5% in 2025Q2 and Saudi unemployment rose from 6.3% to 6.8%, so labour reform progress is not a monotonic quarterly improvement.
The IMF outlook remains highly uncertain and explicitly identifies prolonged shipping disruption, tighter financial conditions and weaker demand as downside risks to growth and diversification.

PIF's preliminary 2025 AUM near US$909bn is below the 2025 Vision 2030 target shown in the annual report, reinforcing that balance-sheet scale alone does not establish successful productive diversification.
limitations: The IMF 2026 macro path is a projection conditioned on gradual normalization of Hormuz traffic and can change materially with conflict duration and oil volumes/prices.
The route map is a transmission/mechanism visual, not a geospatial or capacity model; current pipeline, terminal and shipping utilization must be reverified in time-sensitive use.
The PIF asset figure is explicitly preliminary for 2025 and does not by itself measure project returns, private-sector crowding-in or productive additionality.
Labour statistics cited are 2025Q2 structural context rather than a current 2026 labour-market snapshot.

en.title: Saudi Arabia: oil buffers, state-led diversification and the limits of substitution
en.deck: Saudi Arabia is using hydrocarbon income, state capital and logistics redundancy to widen its productive base, but fiscal dependence, private-sector productivity, labour segmentation and Gulf geography still constrain the transition.
en.regime: State-led diversification remains supported by oil income and large balance sheets while conflict and higher financing costs increase pressure for selective investment and private-sector productivity.
en.key_risk: A prolonged regional disruption or weaker project returns could force sharper prioritization before private investment and non-oil revenue are deep enough to sustain the investment cycle.

pt-BR.title: Arábia Saudita: amortecedores do petróleo, diversificação liderada pelo Estado e os limites da substituição
pt-BR.deck: A Arábia Saudita usa renda de hidrocarbonetos, capital estatal e redundância logística para ampliar sua base produtiva, mas dependência fiscal, produtividade privada, segmentação do trabalho e geografia do Golfo ainda limitam a transição.
pt-BR.regime: A diversificação liderada pelo Estado continua sustentada pela renda do petróleo e por grandes balanços, enquanto conflito e financiamento mais caro aumentam a pressão por investimento seletivo e produtividade privada.
pt-BR.key_risk: Uma interrupção regional prolongada ou retornos menores dos projetos podem exigir priorização mais forte antes que investimento privado e receita não petrolífera sejam suficientes para sustentar o ciclo de investimento.
